scores.reason: 为该局翻盘故事建立主角、四名队友、对手阵容、峡谷场景和战斗规则等圣经内容，服务于当前故事的构造与后续写作，任务相关；不据此认可每项游戏设定的事实正确性。

items.name: Sable
items.description: IGN "Sable", blue-side jungler on Rengar. Builds pure damage — lethality, crit, armor penetration, no defensive item — so one combo either erases a squishy or leaves him dead. Twelve-year-old mouse with a chipped button, instant coffee between games, a jaw that clicks when he is calculating. Speaks in timers and short calls; treats every fight as a clock he has to beat.
invariants: Full-damage build only; Sable never buys defensive items.

items.name: Bram
items.description: Top laner on Ornn. A man in his forties with a smoker going in the yard; discusses brisket temperatures and his lawn while last-hitting, counts minions out loud, and says "we scale" every time the team is behind. Slow, calm, immovable voice. Never tilts, never types in all chat, and quietly takes every side lane nobody else will look at.
invariants: Bram never tilts and never forfeits.

items.name: Priya
items.description: Mid laner on Viktor, a nursing student on night shifts. Her building's power cut at 12:00 and her client dropped; she is gone exactly fifteen minutes and comes back at 27:00 apologizing in caps. Speaks in hospital metaphors — triage, vitals, code blue. Wants a surrender vote when she returns, then becomes the calmest voice on the team. Lives and dies by the gravity cage and the Death Ray.
invariants: Priya's disconnect lasts fifteen minutes of game clock.

items.name: Bex
items.description: ADC on Sivir, playing on a laptop trackpad with a cat named Wonton walking over the keyboard. 0/7 before the comeback. Apologizes constantly in chat ("my b", "sorry sorry"), overextends for one extra minion, and still has the best hands on the team once the panic stops. Sivir's On the Hunt is blue's only speed button and the key to every winning push.
invariants: Bex is heavily behind before the comeback.
Bex plays on a trackpad with a cat wandering the desk.

items.name: Moth
items.description: Support on Lulu. Hyper-competitive teenager with a spreadsheet tracking enemy summoner-spell timers, called out to the second. Refuses to type "gg" before the nexus actually falls, keeps a lucky coin balanced on the monitor, takes one loud breath before every objective, and hates a wasted spell more than a lost fight.
invariants: Moth never forfeits and never types "gg" early.

items.name: Summoner's Rift, night queue
items.description: Three lanes and two rivers, a Baron pit that opens at 20:00, Elder Dragon territory beyond. Blue base has two nexus turrets standing behind its inhibitors; red base mirrors it. Fog of war decides most fights: one missing ward turns a clean push into a slaughter, and the width of the lane mouth is the difference between a siege and a death trap.
invariants: Three lanes, inhibitors, and two nexus turrets per base.

items.name: Match economics and clock
items.description: Kills, assists, towers, inhibitors and neutral monsters all pay gold; bounties grow on a streak, so the losing team can harvest a fortune from one fed enemy. Baron Nashor appears at 20:00 and grants a team-wide buff plus empowered minions. A destroyed inhibitor pumps super minions down that lane until it rebuilds. The clock runs in minutes and seconds and is the spine of every decision in the story.
invariants: Timers are quoted as mm:ss and stay consistent.
Baron buff empowers minions and hands the pushing team the initiative.

items.name: Full-damage Rengar
items.description: Lethality and crit with no defensive item, so the engage window is one leap. Thrill of the Hunt reveals the nearest enemy and lets Sable leap from camouflage with bonus ferocity; a full-ferocity combo deletes a squishy in under a second. If the combo misses, or a shield or spell shield eats it, Sable dies almost instantly. Every ult is a single-use key, never a sustained fight.
invariants: Each ult creates one kill window and offers no second chance.
Sable dies when his engage is spoiled.

items.name: Red team and its late-game ceiling
items.description: Red: Renekton top, Lee Sin jungle, Talon mid, Draven ADC, Pyke support. Their win condition is picks and Baron pressure in the first half. Late they have no reliable ranged waveclear, every engage tool is single-target (kick, hook, dash), and shields or a spell shield spoil the combo. Renekton's damage falls off, Draven must catch axes to keep his, Pyke's resets need kills that stop coming, and Talon cannot leave after a dive. They cannot siege a grouped base.
invariants: Red's engage tools are single-target only.
Red has no sustained ranged waveclear for super minions.

items.name: The comeback line
items.description: Blue loses a Baron fight, gives up an inhibitor, and defends three super-minion sieges. Each Rengar ult converts into one kill and one objective, and the gap closes on bounties and picks rather than on a single miracle fight. The arc ends with a backdoored second inhibitor and a push under the nexus turrets.

items.name: Sable's seat
items.description: First person, past tense, from the jungler's chair: the reader only sees what Sable's screen, his team's comms and his map awareness allow. Timers, gold counts and respawn clocks are used as beats, and every teammate is characterized through the voice coming down the voice chat.

items.name: Bex and Moth, lane partners
items.description: Moth tracks Bex's summoner spells and calls his overextensions a half second before they happen; Bex apologizes and does it anyway. Their trust is rebuilt during the super-minion sieges, when a landed spell shield matters more than any apology.

chapters.title: Ten Seconds of Gray Screen
points: Sable respawns at 26:12 into a base under Baron buff: 6–19 on kills, nine thousand gold behind, Priya's client dark since 12:00.
Bram counts minions out loud while tanking at the tier-two tower; Moth rattles off timers; Bex apologizes for his seventh death.
First ult: Draven steps past his own ward to catch an axe at the river mouth, and Sable deletes him in one leap.
The Baron push stalls, but Renekton and Lee Sin crack the mid inhibitor before the wave breaks — super minions are coming.

chapters.title: Fifteen Minutes
points: Wave one of super minions hits mid and the team discovers how little waveclear it has without Viktor.
Priya reconnects at 27:00 in caps, apologizing, and immediately asks for a surrender vote; Moth refuses to type gg.
Sable's second ult picks Pyke at the inhibitor; the wave breaks with the nexus untouched but two turrets bleeding.
Priya's cage buys the first clean disengage and the team settles on Bram's mantra: we scale.

chapters.title: Wave Two
points: Red returns with a fresh Baron buff and a second super wave; Talon's dive dies on Ornn's knockup.
Sable trades his own life for Draven and Lee Sin, and the gold gap shrinks to four thousand on bounties.
Red's flaws surface under pressure: single-target engage, no ranged waveclear while grouped, Renekton's fury spent on minions.
Red takes another Baron at 32:00 while the third super wave forms, and the base braces for the worst of it.

chapters.title: The Third Wave
points: The hardest siege: super minions and Baron buff in mid, a sideline wave climbing top.
Bex lands the spell shield that eats Pyke's hook and clears a wave without dying; Moth's calls go quiet and exact.
Sable's fourth ult kills Draven beside his own nexus turret and the wave finally dies at the turrets.
The base holds with the nexus exposed, and the team decides to step outside.

chapters.title: Out
points: Blue pushes out on three lanes, wins the river fight, and secures Baron at 35:40.
Priya's cage splits Red at the pit; Bram walks a super wave down mid alone, counting it.
With the buff, blue takes top tier two and the top inhibitor — the first one — and Red's nexus turrets come live.
Red respawns and blue backs off with seconds of Baron still ticking.

chapters.title: Their Late Game
points: Blue converts the Baron into mid tier two and two picks; Red turtles behind its nexus turrets.
Red's late-game ceiling shows: Renekton's damage gone, Draven's axes caught by nobody, Talon stranded after his dive.
A straight five-on-five siege costs blue three lives for nothing, and Sable admits the turrets cannot be cracked head-on.
Priya offers the alternative: bait Baron, and let Sable take the second inhibitor alone.

chapters.title: The Second Inhibitor
points: Moth's script: four of blue show at Baron while Sable waits in red's bottom jungle behind a control ward.
Bex's On the Hunt sells the bait; Red takes it and rotates to the pit, Renekton's recall already spent.
Sable backdoors the bottom inhibitor with eight seconds of vision and a stopwatch in his ear.
The second inhibitor falls, two lanes turn into super minions, and Red's base begins dying from the inside.

chapters.title: Nexus Turrets
points: Blue walks in behind two super waves; the first nexus turret falls and Red's last stand begins.
Deaths trade both ways as Bex's speed button carries blue under the second turret and Moth lands every shield.
Sable's final ult erases Draven at the nexus while Priya's Death Ray cuts the wave behind them.
The nexus falls, the win screen arrives, and Moth types gg at last.
